definitions.explanation: Refusing to change one's mind or yield to others' opinions, even when it would be reasonable to do so. Carries a negative connotation.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{強情|ごうじょう}で{人|ひと}の{話|はなし}を{聞|き}かない。
examples.english: He's stubborn and won't listen to others.

examples.japanese: {強情|ごうじょう}を{張|は}らないで、{素直|すなお}に{謝|あやま}りなさい。
examples.english: Stop being stubborn and apologize honestly.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{昔|むかし}から{強情|ごうじょう}な{性格|せいかく}で、{一度|いちど}{決|き}めたら{絶対|ぜったい}に{曲|ま}げない。
examples.english: My grandfather has always been headstrong — once he decides something, he never backs down.

notes:
USAGE:
Negative nuance — describes someone who unreasonably refuses to compromise. The set phrase {強情|ごうじょう}を{張|は}る (to insist stubbornly) is very common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {強情|ごうじょう}を{張|は}る (to be obstinate; to dig in one's heels)
- {強情|ごうじょう}な{人|ひと} (a stubborn person)
- {強情|ごうじょう}な{性格|せいかく} (a stubborn personality)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {頑固|がんこ}: stubborn; obstinate — similar but can be used more neutrally or even positively (principled)
- {意地|いじ}っ{張|ぱ}り: willful; obstinate — more colloquial, often used about children
